payload.reason: One proposal (practice), selected as the core. Two seams were redesigned against the spikes: how RuleCases chooses its run root, and where the read-only fallback is proved. Nothing in this design has been contested by a second designer.
payload.selection_rationale:
Only one proposal came in, so selection meant checking each of its pieces against what the survey and the five spikes measured.

The bug report contained nothing beyond its title, so two readings were assumed:
- "RuleCases.ps1 is not touched by this slice" is SL-091's validation note explaining why the fix was filed. It does not limit SL-098. The acceptance command runs the real RuleCases.ps1, and the failure comes from its lines :182 and :859, so no fix can leave the file alone.
- "Make both scripts independent of the engine's TEMP" means they pass under both C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and a listable TEMP. It does not mean they ignore TEMP.

Pieces kept as proposed, each resting on a measurement:
1. The removal helper is spike 4's measured route. [IO.Directory]::Delete removed a 20-item tree directly in the real C:\WINDOWS\TEMP under pwsh 7.6.6 and under 5.1, and with only that fix applied the bug test, C-004 and C-006 passed. The helper adds the read-only fallback that spike 4's own no-go asked for: it clears +R on explicit paths found by walking the folder's own contents, which works, while attrib /s does not.
2. The B-008 pad is spike 2's go. A fixed 250-character root gave a length of 428 under both TEMPs, against 384 and 402 unpadded.
3. Routing SyncRootRig through TempTree is spike 5's go: routed parent created first, then Sweep. Under both TEMPs nothing threw, the dead-pid root was swept and the live one kept.
4. The harness child's TEMP is not redirected. The proposal flagged redirecting it as over-engineering against its own interest: spikes 1 and 3 only ever redirected C-001..C-006, never the dotnet-building cases C-007..C-014. That flag was taken as a real signal.

Pieces changed:
1. The run-root predicate. Spike 3's constraint requires either a listability test or adding the .NET delete. Spike 1's no-go named a third option: put the run folder directly in the chosen TEMP so no shared base exists. This design takes that third option and keys the choice on TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's own rule (TEMP at or under the Windows folder means %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp). The proposal's listability test is not used, for three reasons:
   - one predicate then governs TempTree, the WindowCases mirror and RuleCases;
   - under the bug test's unlistable TEMP outside Windows, RuleCases' own root still sits in that TEMP, so the acceptance test keeps exercising both failing sites (:182 and the finally) through the helper;
   - the proposal's must-verify invariant (that the bug test needs no RuleCases folders in its TEMP) stops mattering.
2. The acceptance test is committed unchanged. The proposal added a read-only file to its stand-in; here the helper's shapes (read-only file, junction to an outside folder, already gone, file held open) go into a sibling test instead. The engine's recorded acceptance test stays comparable with the repro's captured failure.

Gaps in earlier stages:
- The build-check could not find the engine interpreter because it searched only C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3. Spikes 1, 3 and 4 used %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe. Derived 3 is therefore runnable, and is a case here rather than a gap.
- Derived 7 (the opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT rig under the engine's TEMP) is checked_by person in the survey and is filed for the person.

components.name: Remove-ScratchDir
components.responsibility: The only way RuleCases removes a scratch folder. If [IO.Directory]::Exists(path) is false, it does nothing. Otherwise it calls [IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $true). If that throws, it walks the folder's own contents with DirectoryInfo.EnumerateFileSystemInfos and clears ReadOnly on every entry that is not a reparse point; it neither descends into reparse points nor touches their attributes. It then waits about 250 ms and calls Delete once more. The removal counts as done when Exists is false afterwards. If the folder is still there, it calls Check $false "cleanup: <path>: <message>". It never throws and prints nothing on success, so existing ok counts are unchanged. A comment names the outside defect it avoids: PowerShell's Remove-Item lists the parent through IsReparsePointLikeSymlink and throws a terminating Win32Exception(5) when the parent cannot be listed.
components.key_interactions: Called from Invoke-HarnessRaw (replacing :181-182) and from Main's finally (replacing :859). Uses the existing Check function, so anything left behind is counted before the summary block at :862-866.

components.name: Get-ScratchParent and the per-run root
components.responsibility: Applies TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's path rule. If [IO.Path]::GetTempPath() is at or under [Environment]::GetFolderPath('Windows') (ordinal ignore-case, on a separator boundary), the parent is $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp. If LOCALAPPDATA is blank, not fully qualified, or itself under the Windows folder, it throws a named refusal: 'RuleCases needs a temp folder outside the Windows folder: TEMP is <..>, LOCALAPPDATA\Temp is <..>'. Otherwise the parent is GetTempPath() itself. On its first call, New-TempDir (:70-75) creates $script:ScratchRoot = <parent>\fsa-rulecases-<10 hex> directly in that parent, with no shared fsa-tests base, and prints one line 'scratch: <root>'. All New-TempDir folders are created inside the root and still recorded in $script:Temps. A run that makes no scratch, such as C-001, creates no root.
components.key_interactions: Under the engine's C:\WINDOWS\TEMP the root goes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-rulecases-<hex>, where a killed run's leftovers can be found (#373, Q-132). Under the bug test's deny-list TEMP, which is outside Windows, the root sits directly in that unlistable TEMP and is removed by Remove-ScratchDir, the shape spike 1 recommended.

components.name: Invoke-HarnessRaw harness-scratch cleanup
components.responsibility: Keeps the 'scratch kept at' regex (:177) and the (GetTempPath(), $env:TEMP) leaf lookup (:179-180). Replaces Test-Path + Remove-Item (:181-182) with Remove-ScratchDir. The harness child keeps its inherited TEMP and TMP, so its mkdtemp folder still sits in the inherited TEMP. .NET Delete removes it there even when that TEMP cannot be listed (measured).
components.key_interactions: This is the site that stopped C-006, C-007, C-008, C-009, C-012 and C-014 with 'Access is denied.'

components.name: Main finally cleanup
components.responsibility: Runs Remove-ScratchDir over every $script:Temps entry without stopping, then over $script:ScratchRoot if it was created. The finally can no longer throw, so the summary block always runs.
components.key_interactions: This is the site that ended C-004 (parity only) and every other run that made scratch with exit 1 and no summary line.

components.name: Acceptance test, committed unchanged
components.responsibility: tests/bugs/SL-098-RuleCasesUnlistableTemp.Tests.ps1 is committed byte-identical to what the repro stage wrote, and its command exiting 0 is the acceptance criterion. Neither its stand-in nor its four checks change.
components.key_interactions: Exercises Remove-ScratchDir at both call sites under an unlistable parent: the stand-in's fsa-rules-* folder through :182, and RuleCases' own fsa-rulecases-<hex> root through the finally.

components.name: Temp-roots shape test
components.responsibility: New engine-free test in the tests/bugs idiom, with no Pester. It parses tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 and tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile and defines Remove-ScratchDir and Get-CloudRigParent from their FunctionDefinitionAst text, with a stub Check that records calls. For Remove-ScratchDir it builds trees inside a Deny-ListDirectory parent under the user's temp: one with a read-only file; one with a junction to an outside folder that holds a read-only file; one that is already gone; one with a file held open with FileShare.None. It asserts each outcome. For Get-CloudRigParent it calls the function in child pwsh processes with TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and with a TEMP outside Windows. Cleanup removes the deny ACE and deletes through .NET, and the test checks that it left nothing.
components.key_interactions: This is where spike 4's read-only fallback and the junction-safety guarantee are proved, since the acceptance test's stand-in has neither shape. It uses the AST-extraction route that SL-088 kept as a repo test.

components.name: Test-B008 fixed-length root
components.responsibility: Line 2210 becomes $pad = 250 - $case.Length - 1. If $pad -lt 1 it throws a named refusal ('B-008 case folder too long for a 250-character root: <case>'). Otherwise the root is Join-Path $case (('long-path-' * 30).Substring(0, $pad)). If Test-R001 already has a pad helper (#368), its idiom is used instead. The file stays ASCII-only with CRLF line endings (#91).
components.key_interactions: New-CaseFolder (:241-250) and Remove-CaseFolder (:329-333) are unchanged. The >400 check at :2220 then sees 428 under any TEMP (spike 2).

components.name: Get-CloudRigParent and the fsa-cf-* listings
components.responsibility: A short function mirroring TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot. If TEMP is at or under GetFolderPath('Windows') it returns $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\fsa-tests, otherwise <TEMP>\fsa-tests. It refuses as TempTree does when LOCALAPPDATA is unusable, and a comment cites TempTree.cs:54-68. The GetDirectories(GetTempPath(), 'fsa-cf-*') calls at :5680 and :5747 (as named in the investigation) list Get-CloudRigParent instead, and return an empty list when that folder does not exist.
components.key_interactions: Moving the rig's roots into fsa-tests would otherwise leave these listings looking in the old place under every TEMP, and they already throw under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. The builder reads both sites first. If they turn out not to look for SyncRootRig's roots, they are left alone and filed.

components.name: TempTree.DefaultTestsRoot()
components.responsibility: New internal static method returning ChooseTestsRoot(Path.GetTempPath(), GetFolderPath(Windows), GetFolderPath(LocalApplicationData)). The default constructor (:32-36) calls it instead of passing the three values inline. It does not create the folder. No new Fact: the existing TempTreeRootTests cover the default constructor, which now goes through it.
components.key_interactions: TempTree.cs is already exempt from the %SystemRoot%\Temp fitness rule, so the GetTempPath and Windows-folder spellings stay in one exempt file.

components.name: SyncRootRig constructor
components.responsibility: Lines 286-290 become: parent = TempTree.DefaultTestsRoot(); Directory.CreateDirectory(parent); swept = CloudRig.Sweep(parent, CloudRig.IsRunning, Unregister, output.WriteLine); Root = Path.Combine(parent, CloudRig.RootName(pid, guid)). The comment that e885d7d added at :282-285 is rewritten to say the rig roots in TempTree's choice, without spelling any of the rule's patterns. CloudRig.cs is unchanged.
components.key_interactions: This is spike 5's measured call pattern. fsa-cf-<pid>-<32 hex> roots now share %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests with TempTree's 32-hex folders. Sweep matches only ^fsa-cf-<pid>-<32 hex>$, so it never touches them.

components.name: Fitness rule exemption removal
components.responsibility: Removes tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CloudPlaceholderTests.cs from except_files (.taad/fitness.yaml:1153-1158) and the exemption sentence from `because` (:1152). Before editing, the builder greps ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.cs, SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json and eng/rules-harness for any pin of that list and changes them in the same commit (#388).
components.key_interactions: With the exemption gone, the rule itself guards the routing, because the opt-in rig never runs in the default suite. RuleCases C-001/C-003 recount settled entries (SL-069), so the two settled rules this design appends must also leave them green.

key_decisions.decision: SL-098 edits tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1. The brief's 'RuleCases.ps1 is not touched by this slice' is read as SL-091's filing note, not as a limit on this slice.
key_decisions.rationale: The acceptance command runs the real RuleCases.ps1, and the captured failure comes from its :182 and :859. The bug report has nothing beyond the title, so this reading is an assumption, recorded as one.

key_decisions.decision: Every scratch removal in RuleCases goes through Remove-ScratchDir: [IO.Directory]::Delete; on failure, clear ReadOnly from a walk of the folder's own contents that skips reparse points, pause briefly, retry once; anything still there becomes a counted 'cleanup:' FAIL. Remove-Item is not used.
key_decisions.rationale: Remove-Item's IsReparsePointLikeSymlink lists the parent and throws a terminating Win32Exception(5) that -ErrorAction cannot suppress (investigation, spike 4 control). .NET Delete does not list the parent (survey item 13, spike 4 Part 1, both shells). Spike 4's no-go was a read-only file, so the fallback is required. Skipping reparse points keeps the attribute walk inside scratch. A leftover is counted rather than hidden because 'leaves none of its folders' is the criterion, and silent leftovers are how Q-132's leak went unseen.

key_decisions.decision: RuleCases' own scratch goes into one per-run root, fsa-rulecases-<10 hex>, created on first use directly in the parent chosen by TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's rule (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when TEMP is at or under the Windows folder, otherwise TEMP). There is no fsa-tests base, the root is removed last in the finally, and its path is printed once.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 1's no-go was a shared base left in the unlistable TEMP, and it suggested this exact no-base shape. Spike 3 found the path rule does not move an unlistable TEMP outside Windows. Here that does not matter, because the helper removes the root there. Sharing TempTree's predicate keeps one root rule across Core tests, WindowCases and RuleCases, and keeps the acceptance test exercising the finally's removal under an unlistable parent. Under the engine's TEMP, a killed run's leftovers become findable (#373, Q-132). The printed path lets the validator check by name. The root can be dropped without touching the helper.

key_decisions.decision: The harness child's TEMP and TMP are not redirected.
key_decisions.rationale: Redirecting would change the environment of every dotnet build the harness runs (harness.py:198-211). C-007..C-014 were never spiked that way. Build-server and MSBuild-node processes may also outlive the run while holding a TEMP that is deleted at its end. The harness scratch is already handled by the helper at :182. Routing it to a listable root is filed as a later slice.

key_decisions.decision: The acceptance test is committed unchanged. The helper's shapes (read-only file, junction to an outside folder, already gone, held-open file) are proved in a new sibling test, tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1, which extracts the function through the PowerShell AST.
key_decisions.rationale: Keeping the engine's acceptance test byte-identical keeps its result comparable with the repro's captured failure. RuleCases.ps1 runs Main when loaded, so AST extraction is the only engine-free way to feed the helper the shapes it branches on (SL-088 kept this route as a repo test).

key_decisions.decision: Test-B008's root is padded to a fixed 250 characters, with a named refusal if the case folder is too long for that.
key_decisions.rationale: Spike 2 was a go: length 428 under both TEMPs, against 384 (fail) and 402 (pass) unpadded. The pad removes the dependence on TEMP instead of hiding it by pointing TEMP elsewhere, which #368 records as having misled the guard.

key_decisions.decision: SyncRootRig takes its parent from a new TempTree.DefaultTestsRoot(), creates it, then sweeps it. CloudRig.cs is unchanged. Stale fsa-cf-* roots left in the old location (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp directly) are no longer swept; clearing them once is filed for the person.
key_decisions.rationale: This is spike 5's measured call pattern. Keeping the GetTempPath and Windows-folder spellings in TempTree.cs, which is already exempt, lets CloudPlaceholderTests.cs come off the exemption list. A legacy sweep would need a GetTempPath spelling back in an exempt file, or an API whose only job is dodging the rule.

key_decisions.decision: CloudPlaceholderTests.cs is removed from the %SystemRoot%\Temp fitness rule's except_files and from its `because` text, together with any pin of that list.
key_decisions.rationale: The exemption's own text (fitness.yaml:1152) says it lasts until this routing lands. Once it is gone the rule is the default-suite regression guard for the routing, because the rig is opt-in and run by a person.

key_decisions.decision: WindowCases' fsa-cf-* listings (:5680, :5747) list the rig's new parent through Get-CloudRigParent, a PowerShell mirror of ChooseTestsRoot, and return nothing when that parent does not exist.
key_decisions.rationale: Moving the rig's roots into fsa-tests would otherwise leave these listings silently looking in the old place under every TEMP, and they already throw under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (investigation). The mirror's output is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests under both measured TEMPs, and the sibling test pins it.

key_decisions.decision: The PowerShell Remove-Item defect is avoided in development scripts only, so it does not become a KnownWorkarounds entry or an app setting.
key_decisions.rationale: The defect is outside the project (PowerShell's FileSystemProvider; no upstream fix for native 5, per the investigation). But the precaution lives in tests/rules, which no app user runs, and it changes no result: the folder is deleted either way, and nothing is skipped, refused or counted differently. A toggle that restores Remove-Item would only restore the crash. The helper's comment names the defect and where it lives so the reason survives. The app's KnownWorkarounds list is untouched.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Kept as proposed: the .NET-delete helper with its read-only fallback (spike 4 plus its own remedy), no redirect of the harness child (the proposal's over-engineering flag, taken as a real signal), the B-008 pad (spike 2), SyncRootRig through TempTree.DefaultTestsRoot (spike 5), and the exemption removal. Changed: (1) the run root is keyed on TempTree's path rule and placed directly in the chosen parent, instead of the proposal's listability probe; (2) the acceptance test stays byte-identical, and the read-only, junction, already-gone and held-open shapes move to a sibling AST-extraction test instead of a read-only file in the acceptance stand-in. (3) The proposal's contract claimed that putting Remove-Item back at :859 makes the bug test fail. Under its own listability design that is not true, because RuleCases' folders would sit in a listable place. Under this design, putting Remove-Item back inside the helper fails both sites.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition to check, and nothing here has yet survived a disagreement with another designer. The reviewer is the first to argue with it.

Seams checked inside the proposal itself, and what changed:
(1) Two root predicates. The proposal chose RuleCases' root with a listability probe, while its WindowCases mirror and TempTree use the path rule (TEMP at or under the Windows folder). Under the bug test's unlistable TEMP outside Windows, the two disagree. RuleCases was moved onto the path rule, with the run root directly in the chosen parent and no base, which is spike 1's suggested shape. One predicate now governs TempTree, Get-CloudRigParent and Get-ScratchParent.
(2) The proposal's contract claimed a mutation at :859 fails the acceptance test. With its listability root, RuleCases' own folders would never sit under an unlistable parent in that test, so the claim was false. With the path rule, the root sits in the unlistable TEMP and the meaningful mutation (Remove-Item back inside Remove-ScratchDir) fails both sites.
(3) The proposal edited the acceptance test's stand-in. It is now kept byte-identical and the helper's shapes are proved separately, so the engine's recorded criterion is not moved.
(4) Shared parent. SyncRootRig's fsa-cf-* roots and TempTree's 32-hex folders now share %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests. CloudRig.Sweep matches only ^fsa-cf-<pid>-<32 hex>$, and nothing deletes the fsa-tests base itself (spike 1 saw it persist with 4 unrelated entries). RuleCases' root deliberately stays out of fsa-tests, so it never races TempTree over a base.
(5) Loud cleanup against the non-regression. A failed removal now fails the run where Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue used to hide it. Validate in #274 measured 0 dirs left after normal completion under a listable TEMP, so -Case All should stay green. Derived 3 under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp is the check.
(6) The harness child keeps the inherited TEMP. Its scratch still lands in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and is removed by the helper there (measured). Only a killed run leaves it unfindable, and that is filed rather than half-fixed.
(7) Architecture rules. The two appended rules are untwinned settled rules over .ps1 files. Lesson SL-065 says the engine's fitness blanks only // and /* */, so '#' and <# #> lines in PowerShell are matched as text. Both patterns are therefore line-anchored and exclude anything after a '#', and the builder keeps 'Remove-Item' off non-'#' lines of RuleCases' comment blocks. RuleCases C-001/C-003 recount settled entries (SL-069), so -Case All covers the count change.

No other contradictory invariants were found: one error contract (Check $false, never throw), one ownership model (each script owns its run root; TempTree owns fsa-tests), and no consistency assumptions.

Stage gap: the build-check missed the engine interpreter at %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe, which spikes 1, 3 and 4 used. That stage should have found it.

architecture_rules.name: RuleCases removes nothing with Remove-Item
architecture_rules.because: Remove-Item on a folder whose parent cannot be listed (the engine's C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, or any create-but-not-list TEMP) throws a terminating Win32Exception(5) from IsReparsePointLikeSymlink. -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue does not suppress it, so a case stops and the finally ends the script before its summary line. Every scratch removal goes through Remove-ScratchDir. Aliases (rm, ri, rd, del) are a known gap in this tripwire.

architecture_rules.name: WindowCases never enumerates the temp folder itself
architecture_rules.because: Listing GetTempPath() itself is denied for this user when TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, and it throws (investigation; survey item 5 for the same 'fsa-cf-*' listing). The rig's roots are found through Get-CloudRigParent, and listing a subfolder this user owns is allowed.

cases.shape: The harness exits non-zero and keeps its scratch directly in a TEMP outside the Windows folder that this user can create in but not list. RuleCases' own run root sits in that same TEMP.
cases.why: :182's Remove-Item threw a terminating Win32Exception(5) and the case stopped. The finally's removal of the root is the same call shape under the same unlistable parent. This is the captured failure.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-098-RuleCasesUnlistableTemp.Tests.ps1 exits 0, with its 4 checks ok. The file is committed byte-identical to the repro's.

cases.behaviour: run every RuleCases case under the engine's TEMP
cases.shape: TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. This covers the six harness cases that expect a non-zero harness exit (C-006, C-007, C-008, C-009, C-012, C-014) and the parity-only cases (C-002..C-005), whose own scratch used to sit directly in that TEMP.
cases.why: Parity-only runs also died at :859 (survey: C-004 26 ok, exit 1, 12 folders left). The run root must go to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp through the Windows-folder branch of Get-ScratchParent.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "$env:TEMP=$env:TMP='C:\WINDOWS\TEMP'; pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case All -EnginePython $env:APPDATA\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe -EngineRoot C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend". It must end 'All checks held.' with exit 0, with no line containing 'Access is denied', 'stopped:' or 'cleanup:'. The printed 'scratch:' path must be under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and Test-Path False afterwards.

cases.behaviour: run every RuleCases case with an ordinary TEMP
cases.shape: TEMP=TMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, which this user can list (Derived 3, non-regression).
cases.why: This was never run, because the build-check found no interpreter. The root moves scratch one level deeper, cleanup failures are now counted instead of silently left, and C-001/C-003 recount settled entries after the two appended rules.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "$env:TEMP=$env:TMP=\"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\"; pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case All -EnginePython $env:APPDATA\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe -EngineRoot C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend". It must end 'All checks held.' with exit 0, with no 'stopped:' or 'cleanup:' line, and the printed 'scratch:' folder must be gone afterwards.

cases.shape: The tree holds a read-only file, and the folder's parent cannot be listed.
cases.why: Spike 4: Directory.Delete(path,$true) threw UnauthorizedAccessException on a +R file and left the tree, while Remove-Item -Force had not stopped on that. The clear-and-retry branch exists only for this.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1. Its check 'a tree with a read-only file is removed under a parent that cannot be listed' is ok, with no Check $false recorded.

cases.check: tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 check 'a junction inside scratch is unlinked and its target is untouched'. Afterwards the scratch is gone, and the outside file still exists and is still ReadOnly.

cases.why: The Exists guard. The harness may already have removed its scratch, or a folder recorded in $script:Temps may never have been created.
cases.check: tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 check 'a missing folder is a no-op': no throw and no Check call.

cases.check: tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 check 'a held file yields one cleanup FAIL and no throw'. The handle is then released and the tree removed by the test's own cleanup.

cases.shape: TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, where the case folder is 65 characters.

cases.shape: The process TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, which this user cannot list.
cases.why: CloudRig.Sweep's EnumerateDirectories(GetTempPath(), 'fsa-cf-*') is denied there (survey item 5). The routing and the exemption removal must leave the rule, its corpus and the default-suite guards green.

Then %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe eng/rules-harness/harness.py --engine-root C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend --scenario all exits 0, and eng/rules-parity.ps1 prints AGREE under both pwsh and powershell.exe.

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Python test tooling on Windows (pytest's tmp_path_factory / rm_rf and shutil.rmtree's read-only handler)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Keep scratch out of a hostile shared temp by making one per-run folder under a temp the user owns. Delete it as a whole, with an error handler that clears the read-only bit and retries.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Selected in part. The chmod-and-retry handler carries over directly: spike 4's no-go is exactly rmtree's read-only failure on Windows. The per-run folder carries over without pytest's shared per-user base, because spike 1 showed a shared base is left behind in an unlistable TEMP. pytest's practice of pointing child processes at the base is not carried over, because the children here run dotnet builds that were never spiked under a redirect. The parent is chosen by TempTree's existing path rule instead of pytest's fixed base.

invariants.precondition: The parent chosen for the run root is writable by this user, and the root inside it can be listed by its owner.
invariants.evidence: Spikes 3 and 5 created and removed folders in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp under both TEMPs. Under the bug test's deny-list TEMP, RuleCases already creates folders (survey), and owned children are listable (spike 4: the recursive Delete enumerated them).

invariants.precondition: Deleting a folder does not require listing that folder's parent.
invariants.evidence: Survey item 13 (deny-list parent) and spike 4 Part 1 (the real C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, pwsh 7.6.6 and 5.1): [IO.Directory]::Delete removed the tree, and Exists was False afterwards.

invariants.precondition: A read-only file blocks the recursive delete, and clearing the flag on explicit paths found by walking the folder's own contents unblocks it.
invariants.evidence: Spike 4: the -ro tree threw UnauthorizedAccessException and was left. SetAttributes or attrib -r on the explicit file path, followed by Delete, removed all 6 trees. attrib /s could not, because it lists the parent.

invariants.precondition: The recursive delete and the attribute walk do not cross a junction into folders outside scratch.
invariants.evidence: Recalled .NET behaviour. Settled by the junction shape in tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1.

invariants.precondition: Nothing writes into the run root after the script deletes it.
invariants.evidence: By construction: TEMP and TMP are not redirected, so no harness child or build server inherits the root.

invariants.precondition: No RuleCases case depends on its New-TempDir scratch sitting directly in GetTempPath().
invariants.evidence: Spike 3 ran C-001..C-006 with scratch one level deeper still, and all passed. C-007..C-014 are settled by the two -Case All runs.

prior_art.pattern: A tool enumerating paths terminated with UnauthorizedAccessException from FileSystemEnumerator.CreateRelativeDirectoryHandle. It was filed as a bug and fixed so that denied paths are handled instead of ending the tool. This is the same class as CloudRig.Sweep's uncaught EnumerateDirectories and RuleCases dying in its finally.
Get-ChildItem | Remove-Item under C:\Windows system folders fails with DirUnauthorizedAccessError even when elevated. The pipeline breaks on the listing, not on the delete.
Get-ChildItem reports 'Access is denied' on some folders even from an administrator prompt, because listing rights come from the folder's ACL, not from elevation alone.

Remove-Item -Recurse goes through RemoveDirectoryInfoItem to IsReparsePointLikeSymlink, which calls FindFirstFileEx on the item's own path and so lists the parent. It throws a terminating Win32Exception that -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue does not suppress. There is no upstream fix for native code 5.
prior_art.where: PowerShell/PowerShell issues #16804 and #16123 (FileSystemProvider), as named in this slice's investigation

prior_art.pattern: rmtree on Windows fails on read-only files. The documented remedy is an error handler that makes the path writable and retries.
prior_art.where: Python standard library docs, shutil.rmtree example (remove_readonly)

prior_art.pattern: Per-session scratch directories, deleted with rm_rf, whose error handler makes read-only entries writable and retries.
%SystemRoot%\Temp lets Users create and traverse but not list, by design. The advice is to use the user's own temp variable. TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot already applies it.
prior_art.where: bugtraq post of 2007-03-12 on Windows Temp ACLs (named in the investigation record)

outside_claims.claim: For BUILTIN\Users, %SystemRoot%\Temp grants create and traverse but not list: (CI)(S,WD,AD,X), plus CREATOR OWNER full control on what they create. This non-elevated user cannot list C:\WINDOWS\TEMP but owns and can list the folders it creates there.
outside_claims.source: Investigation (icacls in Windows Sandbox 26100; GetDirectories and EnumerateDirectories denied on this PC); survey items 1 and 5; lesson #373 (C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests listable)
outside_claims.if_wrong: The engine's TEMP would not be the trigger, and the run-root branch would be unnecessary (harmless).

outside_claims.claim: In pwsh 7.6.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1, Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue on a folder whose parent cannot be listed throws a terminating System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception(5) from IsReparsePointLikeSymlink and leaves the folder.
outside_claims.source: Investigation evidence 3-5; spike dotnet-delete-under-real-windows-temp, control row
outside_claims.if_wrong: The architecture rule banning Remove-Item in RuleCases would be stricter than needed. The fix would still hold.

outside_claims.claim: [IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $true) removes a tree directly inside an unlistable parent without listing that parent, in pwsh 7.6.6 and in 5.1.
outside_claims.source: Survey command 13; spike dotnet-delete-under-real-windows-temp Part 1 (real C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, 20-item tree, both shells)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Remove-ScratchDir would fail at both sites, and the acceptance test would stay red.

outside_claims.claim: Directory.Delete(path, $true) throws UnauthorizedAccessException when the tree holds a read-only file, and leaves the tree.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The read-only fallback would be dead code (harmless).

outside_claims.claim: Clearing ReadOnly with [IO.File]::SetAttributes on the explicit path of a file inside an owned folder directly in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, then calling Directory.Delete, removes the tree. attrib -r /s cannot, because it lists the parent.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The fallback walk would not unblock read-only trees, and a counted cleanup FAIL would remain.

outside_claims.claim: Enumerating an owned folder's own contents works when its parent cannot be listed.
outside_claims.source: Spike dotnet-delete-under-real-windows-temp (the recursive Delete enumerated 20-item trees directly in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP); survey command 13
outside_claims.if_wrong: The fallback walk would throw. It is inside the helper's try, so the result is a counted FAIL, not a crash.

outside_claims.claim: In .NET 10, Directory.Delete(path, true) removes a junction or directory symlink inside the tree as a link and does not delete the target's contents. FileSystemInfo.Attributes carries ReparsePoint for both kinds.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Scratch removal could delete or change files outside scratch. The helper would need a manual walk that unlinks reparse points first. The junction shape in tests/bugs/SL-098-TempRoots.Tests.ps1 settles it.

outside_claims.claim: Test-Path -PathType Container and [IO.Directory]::Exists return True for an existing child of an unlistable parent.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The helper's Exists guard would skip real folders, and the acceptance test's 'nothing left' check would catch it.

outside_claims.claim: The engine venv's Python tempfile.mkdtemp follows TEMP when TMPDIR is unset, and TMPDIR is unset in this session. Whether the engine's real stage shell sets TMPDIR is unknown (SC-216).
outside_claims.if_wrong: Harness scratch could land outside both GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP, so the unchanged leaf lookup would miss it. That is existing behaviour and stays filed under SC-216.

outside_claims.claim: Padding Test-B008's root to 250 characters makes the stopped-ending title+detail length 428 under both C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, against 384 and 402 unpadded.
outside_claims.source: Spike b008-fixed-length-root (published exe, real hook, 96 DPI)
outside_claims.if_wrong: B-008 would still depend on TEMP, and the two B-008 cases would fail.

outside_claims.claim: CloudRig.Sweep over a created ChooseTestsRoot parent does not throw under either TEMP, sweeps a dead-pid fsa-cf root and keeps a live one. Sweep over GetTempPath() throws UnauthorizedAccessException under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
outside_claims.source: Spike cloudrig-sweep-routed-root (Facts A and B, both TEMPs)
outside_claims.if_wrong: The SyncRootRig routing would not fix Derived 5.

outside_claims.claim: The engine's fitness checker blanks only // and /* */ comments, so '#' and <# #> lines in .ps1 files are matched as text by must_not_match patterns. Its Python regexes accept a leading inline (?m)/(?i) flag.
outside_claims.source: Lesson SL-065 (fitness blanks only // and /* */); SL-087 spike constraint ('(?m) prefix' used in fitness.yaml entries)
outside_claims.if_wrong: If comments were blanked, the line anchors would simply be unnecessary. If inline flags were rejected, the two appended rules would fail to load and would need re-spelling.

outside_claims.claim: MSBuild worker nodes and the dotnet build servers can outlive the build that started them and keep its environment, so redirecting the harness child's TEMP to a folder deleted at run end could break later builds.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Redirecting the child would be safe and could make killed-run harness scratch findable. That is the filed later slice.

outside_claims.claim: Antivirus or indexer scans can briefly hold a newly written file open, so a first delete attempt can fail transiently.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The ~250 ms pause before the retry is unnecessary, but harmless.

taste_disagreements: Run-root predicate. The proposal moved RuleCases' scratch out of any TEMP a probe cannot list. This design uses TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's path rule, so one predicate governs TempTree, WindowCases and RuleCases, and the acceptance test keeps RuleCases' own removal under an unlistable parent in play. A reviewer may prefer the listability probe's generality.

Where the read-only fallback is proved. The proposal added a +R file to the acceptance test's stand-in. This design keeps the acceptance test byte-identical and proves the read-only, junction, already-gone and held-open shapes in a sibling AST-extraction test.

Whether the per-run root belongs in this slice at all. The proposal's own over-engineering note says the delete helper alone passes the acceptance test. The root is kept for findable killed-run leftovers (#373, Q-132) and can be dropped on its own.
Whether a failed scratch removal should fail the run (counted FAIL, exit 1) or only print a warning line.
A PowerShell mirror of ChooseTestsRoot in WindowCases (Get-CloudRigParent) versus hard-coding %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests, which is the same answer under both measured TEMPs.
Stale fsa-cf-* roots in the old location. The person clears them once, versus a legacy sweep kept in exempt TempTree.cs.
